A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and support a reliable comparison. The main text and Appendices A–G can be matched, including equations and proofs; v2 additionally contains Appendix H and Figure 1.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical convergence results, lower bounds, and proofs, including in its appendices. Its references to empirical observations concern other work; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Appendix H reports original numerical simulations comparing two parameter schedules under four heavy-tailed noise settings. Figure 1 presents convergence trajectories averaged over 10 trials.

M1.justification: Appendix E revises prescribed stepsizes: Equations (40), (47), (59), and (61) remove the factor sqrt(1+σ_l^p/G^p) from the relevant stepsize caps. Equation (61) also adds 1 to the denominator defining γ_*. These are limited parameter-rule changes; Algorithms 1 and 2 retain their update structures.

E1.justification: From no empirical task coverage in v1, Appendix H adds one synthetic task: minimizing a 50-dimensional L1-distance objective with independent asymmetric Pareto-based additive noise. Evaluation covers p=1.2, 1.4, 1.6, and 1.8, constituting a limited synthetic expansion.

E2.justification: Liu and Zhou (2023), previously discussed theoretically, becomes an actually evaluated comparator in Appendix H and Figure 1. Its stepsize and clipping schedule are adapted from its Theorem 4 and compared with a schedule derived from this work.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces a simulation protocol absent from v1: zero initialization, a specified target vector, 10,000 iterations, and evaluation of the average-iterate objective gap. Both compared schedules retain only their dominant t^(-1/p) stepsize term and use an anytime implementation.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a numerical sensitivity analysis across four tail parameters, examining how the schedules' comparative behavior depends on p. v1 discusses this dependence theoretically but contains no corresponding numerical analysis.

E5.justification: v2 introduces repeated-run and uncertainty reporting: 10 trials for each schedule and tail setting, with means and standard-error bands. This is a new reporting practice for new simulations, not an increase in runs of an existing experiment.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds comparative convergence curves for four p settings. The proposed schedule achieves lower plotted objective gaps than Liu and Zhou (2023), with particularly close curves at p=1.8. These are new results without an empirical counterpart in v1.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–4 and their full statements in Appendix E remove mixed noise–Lipschitz terms: the convex 1/sqrt(T) term becomes GD/sqrt(T), and the strongly convex 1/T term becomes G²/(µT). Corresponding derivations are revised, and Section 4.2 corrects a logarithmic factor in ρ². The leading rates, core assumptions, and Appendix G's lower-bound proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: refined high-probability analysis, improved in-expectation leading rates, an anytime stabilized variant, and matching in-expectation lower bounds. The finite-time refinements do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: New Remark 9 explains why earlier lower bounds can be surpassed: the additional directional-moment parameter defines a narrower oracle class. Appendix H also interprets the small difference near p=2 through the predicted vanishing advantage. Existing limitations concerning extra terms and high-probability gaps remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds reproducibility information for the new simulations, including the objective and target vector, asymmetric noise generator with Pareto shape p+0.001, initialization, iteration budget, moment-based parameter choices, and both stepsize/clipping formulas.

R1.justification: Remark 9 refines positioning against prior lower-bound research by explicitly comparing the underlying oracle classes. The Sun et al. citation changes from a 2024 preprint to its 2025 journal version; this is the same cited work, not an additional reference.

P1.justification: v2 adds a focused explanatory remark, Appendix H, and a conference-status footnote, alongside small wording and punctuation edits. The existing section order and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 1, a four-panel display with method legends, iteration and objective axes, standard-error bands, and a caption. Existing algorithm displays and the single-column format are retained, with localized page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 tightens finite-time bounds with corresponding derivations and clarifies the apparently conflicting relationship with prior lower bounds through Remark 9. Appendix H adds a documented, repeated-run illustration, although its single synthetic objective and simplified schedules provide limited empirical support. These gains improve precision and clarity while leaving the main theoretical contribution substantially unchanged.
